Proposition
[The plane is not a backward pointwise limit] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iv:page-0119, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iv:page-0120, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iv:page-0121 ↗ lem:chow-iv-distance-circles-near-neck-center ↗ lem:chow-iv-radius-linear-time 1. ch29:29.30\group Backward Geometry

No fixed point $q\in S^2$ can have $(S^2,g(t_i+t),q)$ converge without rescaling to the flat plane as $t_i\to -\infty $.
